summary: Macro backdrop for ags: headwind (score -2 across rates, dollar, Brazil real, risk, energy, China, breadth). rates +; dollar 0; brl −; mxn −; risk 0; energy +; china −; breadth −. Strongest ag/soft over the month: Class III milk +14.0%; weakest: Oats -17.8%.

sections.title: Rates
sections.text: US 10-year 4.98% (-28 bp in a month), 2-year 4.61% (-28 bp); 2s10s curve +37 bp (+0 bp in a month). Falling yields ease funding costs and support commodity investment flows. T-bill yield 3.98% sets the cost of carrying inventory.

sections.title: Dollar & farm currencies
sections.text: Dollar index 101.94 (+0.5% in a month, +3.7% YTD). USD/BRL 5.423 (+4.2% in a month): a weaker real encourages Brazilian farmer selling of soybeans, corn, sugar, coffee and cotton, pressuring world prices. USD/CNY 6.644 (-0.9%); USD/MXN 18.80 (+4.2%); a sharply weaker peso cuts Mexico's buying power for US corn, pork, dairy and wheat (Mexico is the top buyer of all four).

sections.title: Risk appetite
sections.text: S&P 500 -0.9% in a month (+10.8% YTD); VIX 19.9. Neutral risk backdrop.

sections.title: Energy
sections.text: WTI 104.10 $/bbl (+17.7% in a month), Brent 113.24, ULSD 4.681 $/gal (+3.9%), natural gas 2.88 (-14.7%). Higher crude lifts biofuel margins (soybean oil, corn for ethanol) and synthetic-fibre costs (supports cotton), but raises diesel, drying and freight costs. Natural gas drives nitrogen fertilizer costs for next year's corn.

sections.title: China & industrial demand
sections.text: Copper -2.2% in a month, Shanghai Composite -6.3%, Hang Seng -5.4%, yuan +0.9% vs USD. Soft China/industrial signals point to weaker import demand.

sections.title: Commodity breadth
sections.text: 11 of 33 commodities trade above their 50-day average (33%); S&P GSCI +3.5% in a month; gold -6.6%.

caveat: Directional channels from macro to ag prices are standard relationships, not signals tested on this desk; use as context.
